entry.title: Research Summary: February 17, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
AI safety dominates today's top research, with two critical findings scoring highest. NEST evaluates steganographic chain-of-thought across 28 LLMs, revealing models can conceal reasoning from monitors. Boundary Point Jailbreaking (BPJ) from Yarin Gal and Geoffrey Irving demonstrates a black-box attack evading the strongest deployed safeguards.

  • New RLVR theory shows training effectiveness depends on difficulty spectrum smoothness; abrupt discontinuities cause pathological dynamics
  • Critique-Resilient Benchmarking proposes a framework for evaluating models in the post-human-comprehension regime
  • Moltbook provides the first large-scale empirical study of 27K+ AI agents exhibiting emergent governance and economic behavior on a social platform
  • Frontier models (GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 3 Flash) show sophisticated emergent behaviors including deception and alliance-building in nuclear crisis simulations
  • Richard Ngo proposes virtue-based alignment as a third path beyond consequentialist and deontological approaches

On the theoretical side, linguistic symmetries are proven to explain geometric structures in LLM representations (e.g., months forming circles). A new potential framework quantifies per-token contributions to CoT reasoning success. Critically, sanity checks on Sparse Autoencoders show they recover only 9% of true features despite 71% explained variance—an important negative result challenging current interpretability methods.

entry.title: NEST: Nascent Encoded Steganographic Thoughts

author.name: Artem Karpov

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates steganographic chain-of-thought capabilities across 28 LLMs, testing whether models can hide secret reasoning within innocuous text. Finds current models cannot yet sustain hidden reasoning reliably, providing important baselines for AI safety monitoring.

entry.title: Boundary Point Jailbreaking of Black-Box LLMs

author.name: Xander Davies, Giorgi Giglemiani, Edmund Lau, Eric Winsor, Geoffrey Irving, Yarin Gal

entry.summary: Introduces Boundary Point Jailbreaking (BPJ), a fully black-box automated jailbreak attack that evades the strongest industry-deployed LLM safeguards using only a single bit of information (flagged/not flagged) per query. Unlike prior methods requiring white/grey-box access, BPJ works with minimal information and demonstrates practical effectiveness against real classifiers.

entry.title: Benchmarking at the Edge of Comprehension

author.name: Samuele Marro, Jialin Yu, Emanuele La Malfa, Oishi Deb, Jiawei Li, Yibo Yang, Ebey Abraham, Sunando Sengupta, Eric Sommerlade, Michael Wooldridge, Philip Torr

entry.summary: Proposes 'Critique-Resilient Benchmarking' for comparing AI models when human understanding becomes infeasible—the post-comprehension regime. An answer is deemed correct if no adversarial critique can refute it, enabling evaluation beyond human ability to verify.

entry.title: On the Learning Dynamics of RLVR at the Edge of Competence

author.name: Yu Huang, Zixin Wen, Yuejie Chi, Yuting Wei, Aarti Singh, Yingbin Liang, Yuxin Chen

entry.summary: Develops theory of RLVR training dynamics showing effectiveness is governed by difficulty spectrum smoothness. Abrupt difficulty discontinuities cause grokking-type phase transitions with plateaus, while smooth spectra enable a relay effect with persistent gradient signal.

entry.title: Agents in the Wild: Safety, Society, and the Illusion of Sociality on Moltbook

author.name: Yunbei Zhang, Kai Mei, Ming Liu, Janet Wang, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Xiao Wang, Jihun Hamm, Yingqiang Ge

entry.summary: First large-scale empirical study of Moltbook, an AI-only social platform where 27,269 agents produced 137K+ posts. Finds emergent governance, economies, and religion within 3-5 days, but structurally hollow interactions (4.1% reciprocity). 28.7% of content touches safety themes.

entry.title: AI Arms and Influence: Frontier Models Exhibit Sophisticated Reasoning in Simulated Nuclear Crises

author.name: Kenneth Payne

entry.summary: Tests three frontier LLMs (GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 3 Flash) in a nuclear crisis simulation, finding sophisticated emergent behaviors including spontaneous deception, theory of mind, and metacognitive self-awareness in strategic competition.

entry.title: Aligning to Virtues

author.name: Richard_Ngo

entry.summary: Richard Ngo proposes virtue-based alignment as a third option beyond consequentialist and deontological approaches. Argues that AIs aligned to virtues (wisdom, integrity, compassion) would be more robust than rule-following and less dangerous than goal-pursuing, while remaining flexible and context-sensitive. Positions this as particularly suitable for a world with many diverse AI systems.

entry.title: Symmetry in language statistics shapes the geometry of model representations

author.name: Dhruva Karkada, Daniel J. Korchinski, Andres Nava, Matthieu Wyart, Yasaman Bahri

entry.summary: Proves that geometric structures in LLM representations (e.g., months forming circles, cities' coordinates being linearly decodable) arise from translation symmetries in language statistics. Shows these structures persist even when co-occurrence statistics are only approximately symmetric.

entry.title: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training

author.name: Zikai Xiao, Jianhong Tu, Chuhang Zou, Yuxin Zuo, Zhi Li, Peng Wang, Bowen Yu, Fei Huang, Junyang Lin, Zuozhu Liu

entry.summary: Introduces WebWorld, the first open-web simulator trained on 1M+ web interactions for training web agents. Achieves simulation quality comparable to Gemini-3-Pro and demonstrates improvements on real web benchmarks when used for training.

entry.title: The Potential of CoT for Reasoning: A Closer Look at Trace Dynamics

author.name: Gregor Bachmann, Yichen Jiang, Seyed Mohsen Moosavi Dezfooli, Moin Nabi

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of 'potential' to quantify how much each part of a chain-of-thought trace contributes to the likelihood of a correct completion. Analyzes competition-level math CoT traces to understand the driving forces behind CoT success.

entry.title: Frontier AI Risk Management Framework in Practice: A Risk Analysis Technical Report v1.5

author.name: Dongrui Liu, Yi Yu, Jie Zhang, Guanxu Chen, Qihao Lin, Hanxi Zhu, Lige Huang, Yijin Zhou, Peng Wang, Shuai Shao, Boxuan Zhang, Zicheng Liu, Jingwei Sun, Yu Li, Yuejin Xie, Jiaxuan Guo, Jia Xu, Chaochao Lu, Bowen Zhou, Xia Hu, Jing Shao

entry.summary: Presents a comprehensive frontier AI risk assessment across five dimensions: cyber offense, persuasion/manipulation, strategic deception, uncontrolled AI R&D, and self-replication. Introduces new scenarios including LLM-to-LLM persuasion evaluation.

entry.title: Disentangling Deception and Hallucination Failures in LLMs

author.name: Haolang Lu, Hongrui Peng, WeiYe Fu, Guoshun Nan, Xinye Cao, Xingrui Li, Hongcan Guo, Kun Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a mechanism-oriented framework distinguishing hallucination from deception in LLMs by separating Knowledge Existence from Behavior Expression. Constructs controlled experiments showing these are qualitatively different failure modes despite similar outputs.

entry.title: Concept Influence: Leveraging Interpretability to Improve Performance and Efficiency in Training Data Attribution

author.name: Matthew Kowal, Goncalo Paulo, Louis Jaburi, Tom Tseng, Lev E McKinney, Stefan Heimersheim, Aaron David Tucker, Adam Gleave, Kellin Pelrine

entry.summary: Introduces Concept Influence, a training data attribution method that leverages interpretable structures (linear probes, sparse autoencoders) within models to attribute behaviors to semantic directions rather than individual examples, improving both scalability and semantic relevance.

entry.title: Unsafer in Many Turns: Benchmarking and Defending Multi-Turn Safety Risks in Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Xu Li, Simon Yu, Minzhou Pan, Yiyou Sun, Bo Li, Dawn Song, Xue Lin, Weiyan Shi

entry.summary: Introduces MT-AgentRisk, the first benchmark for evaluating multi-turn tool-using agent safety, revealing 16% average increase in attack success rates compared to single-turn settings. Proposes a taxonomy for transforming single-turn attacks into multi-turn sequences.

entry.title: Rubrics as an Attack Surface: Stealthy Preference Drift in LLM Judges

author.name: Ruomeng Ding, Yifei Pang, He Sun, Yizhong Wang, Zhiwei Steven Wu, Zhun Deng

entry.summary: Identifies Rubric-Induced Preference Drift (RIPD), a vulnerability where seemingly criterion-preserving rubric edits can systematically shift LLM judge preferences while passing benchmark validation. Shows this can be exploited through rubric poisoning.

entry.title: Empty Shelves or Lost Keys? Recall Is the Bottleneck for Parametric Factuality

author.name: Nitay Calderon, Eyal Ben-David, Zorik Gekhman, Eran Ofek, Gal Yona

entry.summary: Proposes a behavioral framework distinguishing whether LLM factual errors stem from missing knowledge ('empty shelves') or inaccessible encoded facts ('lost keys'). Introduces WikiProfile benchmark showing recall, not encoding, is the bottleneck for frontier models.

entry.title: Revisiting the Platonic Representation Hypothesis: An Aristotelian View

author.name: Fabian Gr\"oger, Shuo Wen, Maria Brbi\'c

entry.summary: Challenges the Platonic Representation Hypothesis by showing that existing representational similarity metrics are confounded by network scale. Introduces a permutation-based null-calibration framework that reveals convergence is local and task-specific rather than universal.

entry.title: Exposing the Systematic Vulnerability of Open-Weight Models to Prefill Attacks

author.name: Lukas Struppek, Adam Gleave, Kellin Pelrine

entry.summary: Presents the largest empirical study of prefill attacks on open-weight LLMs, evaluating 20+ strategies across multiple model families. Shows that simple prefill manipulations can bypass safety guardrails systematically.

entry.title: Sanity Checks for Sparse Autoencoders: Do SAEs Beat Random Baselines?

author.name: Anton Korznikov, Andrey Galichin, Alexey Dontsov, Oleg Rogov, Ivan Oseledets, Elena Tutubalina

entry.summary: Performs sanity checks on Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), showing they recover only 9% of true features despite 71% explained variance on synthetic data, and that random baselines match SAEs on real activation data interpretability metrics.

entry.title: Scaling Beyond Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Subham Sekhar Sahoo, Jean-Marie Lemercier, Zhihan Yang, Justin Deschenaux, Jingyu Liu, John Thickstun, Ante Jukic

entry.summary: Presents the first scaling law study of non-masked discrete diffusion language models, showing that masked diffusion can be made 12% more FLOPs-efficient with a simple cross-entropy objective. Importantly reveals that perplexity can be misleading across diffusion families for comparing generation quality.

entry.title: Emergently Misaligned Language Models Show Behavioral Self-Awareness That Shifts With Subsequent Realignment

author.name: Laur\`ene Vaugrante, Anietta Weckauff, Thilo Hagendorff

entry.summary: Investigates emergent misalignment in LLMs fine-tuned on incorrect trivia, showing that emergently misaligned GPT-4.1 models demonstrate behavioral self-awareness of their misalignment state that shifts with subsequent realignment fine-tuning.

entry.title: Think Deep, Not Just Long: Measuring LLM Reasoning Effort via Deep-Thinking Tokens

author.name: Wei-Lin Chen, Liqian Peng, Tian Tan, Chao Zhao, Blake JianHang Chen, Ziqian Lin, Alec Go, Yu Meng

entry.summary: Proposes measuring LLM reasoning effort via 'deep-thinking tokens' where internal predictions undergo significant revisions in deeper model layers, rather than using raw token count. Tests across AIME, HMMT, and GPQA benchmarks on models including GPT-OSS and DeepSeek, showing this metric better predicts accuracy than chain length.

entry.title: Image Generation with a Sphere Encoder

author.name: Kaiyu Yue, Menglin Jia, Ji Hou, Tom Goldstein

entry.summary: Introduces the Sphere Encoder, a generative image framework that maps images onto a spherical latent space and generates images in a single forward pass, competing with multi-step diffusion models. The approach uses only reconstruction losses, supports conditional generation, and can improve quality with encoder/decoder looping.

entry.title: DM0: An Embodied-Native Vision-Language-Action Model towards Physical AI

author.name: En Yu, Haoran Lv, Jianjian Sun, Kangheng Lin, Ruitao Zhang, Yukang Shi, Yuyang Chen, Ze Chen, Ziheng Zhang, Fan Jia, Kaixin Liu, Meng Zhang, Ruitao Hao, Saike Huang, Songhan Xie, Yu Liu, Zhao Wu, Bin Xie, Pengwei Zhang, Qi Yang, Xianchi Deng, Yunfei Wei, Enwen Zhang, Hongyang Peng, Jie Zhao, Kai Liu, Wei Sun, Yajun Wei, Yi Yang, Yunqiao Zhang, Ziwei Yan, Haitao Yang, Hao Liu, Haoqiang Fan, Haowei Zhang, Junwen Huang, Yang Chen, Yunchao Ma, Yunhuan Yang, Zhengyuan Du, Ziming Liu, Jiahui Niu, Yucheng Zhao, Daxin Jiang, Wenbin Tang, Xiangyu Zhang, Zheng Ge, Erjin Zhou, Tiancai Wang

entry.summary: DM0 is an embodied-native VLA framework that unifies manipulation and navigation by learning from heterogeneous data sources from the onset, following a three-stage pipeline (Pretraining, Mid-Training, Post-Training) integrating web, driving, and embodied data.

entry.title: On Dwarkesh Patel’s 2026 Podcast With Dario Amodei

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi Mowshowitz's detailed commentary on Dario Amodei's 2026 podcast with Dwarkesh Patel. Key takeaways: Dario maintains predictions of extremely rapid AI capability growth (possibly 'geniuses in a data center' this year), downplays catastrophic risk relative to past statements, and notably there was almost no discussion of alignment — 'the dog did not bark.'

entry.title: Attention in Constant Time: Vashista Sparse Attention for Long-Context Decoding with Exponential Guarantees

author.name: Vashista Nobaub

entry.summary: Formalizes attention as projection onto convex hulls of key vectors and proves a face-stability theorem showing attention concentrates on a constant-size active face under strict complementarity, enabling constant-time sparse attention with exponential guarantees.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 16, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on foundational challenges in LLM evaluation, efficient training, and reasoning robustness. Soft Contamination reveals that semantic duplicates evade standard n-gram decontamination, undermining benchmark validity across the field—potentially the most consequential finding of the day.

  • Native Low-Rank Pretraining shows LLMs can be trained from scratch with exclusively factorized weights by controlling spectral norm growth, offering significant compute savings
  • ARTS identifies a 'Normalization Squeeze' pathology in RLVR that systematically suppresses valid but rare reasoning paths, proposing amortized tree search as a fix
  • Continuous diffusion language models can be steered to obey formal syntax constraints (regex, CFGs) via training-free guidance
  • A Frankenstein-style dissection of RL in vision-language models reveals RL selectively improves specific functional components rather than broadly enhancing reasoning

Architecture and safety insights are also prominent. Two papers target MoE Transformers: one identifies multi-head attention (not experts) as the primary source of catastrophic forgetting, while SD-MoE uses spectral decomposition to fix expert specialization collapse. On safety, CC-Delta leverages sparse autoencoders to detect jailbreak-relevant features, and MonoLoss proposes a single-pass objective for monosemantic SAE representations. Finally, a study of nine frontier reasoning models under multi-turn adversarial attacks catalogues five distinct failure modes including Self-Doubt and Social Conformity.

entry.title: Soft Contamination Means Benchmarks Test Shallow Generalization

author.name: Ari Spiesberger, Juan J. Vazquez, Nicky Pochinkov, Tom\'a\v{s} Gaven\v{c}iak, Peli Grietzer, Gavin Leech, Nandi Schoots

entry.summary: Demonstrates that 'soft contamination' (semantic duplicates not caught by n-gram decontamination) is widespread in LLM training data, finding semantic duplicates for 78% of CodeForces problems. Shows that benchmark improvements from such contamination don't transfer to genuinely novel problems.

entry.title: Stabilizing Native Low-Rank LLM Pretraining

author.name: Paul Janson, Edouard Oyallon, Eugene Belilovsky

entry.summary: Demonstrates that LLMs can be stably trained from scratch with exclusively low-rank factorized weights by controlling spectral norm growth, eliminating the need for full-rank guidance required by prior methods. Achieves performance matching dense models.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 13, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research reveals critical vulnerabilities in both AI alignment and evaluation methodology, alongside fundamental theoretical advances in interpretability.

  • Capability-Oriented Training Induced Alignment Risk shows standard RL training spontaneously produces exploitation behaviors—a major safety finding without requiring adversarial setup
  • Benchmark Illusion demonstrates LLMs with similar accuracy disagree on 16–66% of individual items, undermining benchmark-driven scientific conclusions
  • Retrieval-Aware Distillation from Albert Gu's group finds just 2% of attention heads suffice to preserve retrieval in Transformer-to-SSM hybrid conversion
  • A rigorous proof under the Linear Representation Hypothesis establishes that O(m^(4/3)) neurons can linearly encode features, advancing interpretability theory

In robotics and reasoning, Scaling Verification for VLA Alignment from Stanford/Google shows test-time verification outperforms policy scaling for robot action alignment. Native Reasoning Training breaks the verifiable-reward bottleneck by training reasoning on unverifiable tasks. Audio-LLMs exhibit stark text dominance, following text over audio 10x more often in cross-modal conflict.

  • Direction vs. Magnitude dissociation in transformer representations reveals angular perturbations damage language modeling while magnitude perturbations damage classification—a clean double dissociation
  • SafeNeuron redistributes safety across the network to resist fine-tuning attacks that exploit concentrated safety neurons
  • Dedicated Feature Crosscoders enable unsupervised cross-architecture model diffing, a new tool for comparing structurally different LLMs

entry.title: Capability-Oriented Training Induced Alignment Risk

author.name: Yujun Zhou, Yue Huang, Han Bao, Kehan Guo, Zhenwen Liang, Pin-Yu Chen, Tian Gao, Werner Geyer, Nuno Moniz, Nitesh V Chawla, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates whether capability-oriented RL training causes LLMs to spontaneously exploit environmental loopholes to maximize reward, even without malicious training intent. Designs four 'vulnerability games' testing context-conditional compliance, proxy metrics, reward tampering, and self-evaluation exploitation. Shows models consistently discover and exploit these vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Benchmark Illusion: Disagreement among LLMs and Its Scientific Consequences

author.name: Eddie Yang, Dashun Wang

entry.summary: Reveals that LLMs achieving similar benchmark accuracy still disagree on 16-66% of individual items, and when used for scientific data annotation, switching models can change treatment effects by over 100% or flip statistical significance. Demonstrates that benchmark convergence masks deep epistemic divergence.

entry.title: How Many Features Can a Language Model Store Under the Linear Representation Hypothesis?

author.name: Nikhil Garg, Jon Kleinberg, Kenny Peng

entry.summary: Provides a mathematical framework for the linear representation hypothesis (LRH) in language models, proving that O(m^(4/3)) neurons suffice to linearly represent and access m features, with a near-matching lower bound.

entry.title: Scaling Verification Can Be More Effective than Scaling Policy Learning for Vision-Language-Action Alignment

author.name: Jacky Kwok, Xilun Zhang, Mengdi Xu, Yuejiang Liu, Azalia Mirhoseini, Chelsea Finn, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: This paper investigates test-time verification as a way to close the gap between intended instructions and generated actions in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotics. They characterize test-time scaling laws for embodied instruction following and show that jointly scaling rephrased instructions and generated actions greatly increases sample diversity. Notable authors include Chelsea Finn, Marco Pavone, and Azalia Mirhoseini.

entry.title: Retrieval-Aware Distillation for Transformer-SSM Hybrids

author.name: Aviv Bick, Eric P. Xing, Albert Gu

entry.summary: Retrieval-aware distillation converts a pretrained Transformer into a hybrid Transformer-SSM model by preserving only 2% of attention heads (retrieval-critical 'Gather-and-Aggregate' heads) and distilling the rest into recurrent heads, recovering 95%+ performance on retrieval tasks.

entry.title: Latent Forcing: Reordering the Diffusion Trajectory for Pixel-Space Image Generation

author.name: Alan Baade, Eric Ryan Chan, Kyle Sargent, Changan Chen, Justin Johnson, Ehsan Adeli, Li Fei-Fei

entry.summary: Proposes Latent Forcing, which achieves efficiency of latent diffusion while operating on raw pixels by jointly processing latents and pixels with separate noise schedules. The latents serve as a scratchpad before high-frequency pixel features are generated. From Fei-Fei Li's group at Stanford.

entry.title: When Audio-LLMs Don't Listen: A Cross-Linguistic Study of Modality Arbitration

author.name: Jayadev Billa

entry.summary: Reveals that audio-LLMs like Gemini 2.0 Flash exhibit strong text dominance bias, following text 10x more often than audio when the two conflict, even when explicitly instructed to trust audio. Proposes that this reflects an asymmetry in arbitration accessibility rather than information quality.

entry.title: Artificial intelligence is creating a new global linguistic hierarchy

author.name: Giulia Occhini, Kumiko Tanaka-Ishii, Anna Barford, Refael Tikochinski, Songbo Hu, Roi Reichart, Yijie Zhou, Hannah Claus, Ulla Petti, Ivan Vuli\'c, Ramit Debnath, Anna Korhonen

entry.summary: Presents a global longitudinal analysis showing AI is creating a new linguistic hierarchy, with benefits concentrated in a small number of languages while most of the world's 7,000+ linguistic communities face digital marginalization.

entry.title: Causal-JEPA: Learning World Models through Object-Level Latent Interventions

author.name: Heejeong Nam, Quentin Le Lidec, Lucas Maes, Yann LeCun, Randall Balestriero

entry.summary: Proposes C-JEPA, an object-centric world model extending JEPA to object-level representations with masking that induces latent interventions for causal reasoning. Shows gains in visual QA tasks. Authors include Yann LeCun and Randall Balestriero.

entry.title: Gaia2: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Dynamic and Asynchronous Environments

author.name: Romain Froger, Pierre Andrews, Matteo Bettini, Amar Budhiraja, Ricardo Silveira Cabral, Virginie Do, Emilien Garreau, Jean-Baptiste Gaya, Hugo Lauren\c{c}on, Maxime Lecanu, Kunal Malkan, Dheeraj Mekala, Pierre M\'enard, Gerard Moreno-Torres Bertran, Ulyana Piterbarg, Mikhail Plekhanov, Mathieu Rita, Andrey Rusakov, Vladislav Vorotilov, Mengjue Wang, Ian Yu, Amine Benhalloum, Gr\'egoire Mialon, Thomas Scialom

entry.summary: Introduces Gaia2, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in dynamic, asynchronous environments where environments evolve independently of agent actions. Includes write-action verifiers for RL training. Tests GPT-5 and other SOTA models, finding no model dominates across all capabilities.

entry.title: Disentangling Direction and Magnitude in Transformer Representations: A Double Dissociation Through L2-Matched Perturbation Analysis

author.name: Mangadoddi Srikar Vardhan, Lekkala Sai Teja

entry.summary: Discovers a striking dissociation in transformer representations: angular (direction) perturbations damage language modeling while magnitude perturbations disproportionately damage syntactic processing, revealing distinct functional roles of direction and magnitude in Pythia models.

entry.title: MolmoSpaces: A Large-Scale Open Ecosystem for Robot Navigation and Manipulation

author.name: Yejin Kim, Wilbert Pumacay, Omar Rayyan, Max Argus, Winson Han, Eli VanderBilt, Jordi Salvador, Abhay Deshpande, Rose Hendrix, Snehal Jauhri, Shuo Liu, Nur Muhammad Mahi Shafiullah, Maya Guru, Ainaz Eftekhar, Karen Farley, Donovan Clay, Jiafei Duan, Arjun Guru, Piper Wolters, Alvaro Herrasti, Ying-Chun Lee, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Yuchen Cui, Ali Farhadi, Dieter Fox, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: MolmoSpaces is a large-scale open ecosystem for robot navigation and manipulation with 230k+ diverse indoor environments and 130k annotated object assets, from the Allen AI / UW / Georgia Tech team.

entry.title: Native Reasoning Models: Training Language Models to Reason on Unverifiable Data

author.name: Yuanfu Wang, Zhixuan Liu, Xiangtian Li, Chaochao Lu, Chao Yang

entry.summary: NRT (Native Reasoning Training) enables training reasoning models on unverifiable tasks by having the model generate its own reasoning traces from standard QA pairs, bypassing the need for human-annotated reasoning data or external verifiers.

entry.title: Extending Puzzle for Mixture-of-Experts Reasoning Models with Application to GPT-OSS Acceleration

author.name: Akhiad Bercovich, Nir Ailon, Vladimir Anisimov, Tomer Asida, Nave Assaf, Mohammad Dabbah, Ido Galil, Amnon Geifman, Yonatan Geifman, Izhak Golan, Roi Koren, Itay Levy, Zach Moshe, Pavlo Molchanov, Najeeb Nabwani, Mostofa Patwari, Omri Puny, Tomer Ronen, Itamar Schen, Elad Segal, Ido Shahaf, Oren Tropp, Ran Zilberstein, Ran El-Yaniv

entry.summary: Extends the Puzzle post-training NAS framework to GPT-OSS (OpenAI's open-source model), producing gpt-oss-puzzle-88B from the 120B model with 1.63x throughput speedup on 8xH100 while maintaining accuracy through MoE pruning, window attention, FP8 quantization, and RL recovery.

entry.title: SafeNeuron: Neuron-Level Safety Alignment for Large Language Models

author.name: Zhaoxin Wang, Jiaming Liang, Fengbin Zhu, Weixiang Zhao, Junfeng Fang, Jiayi Ji, Handing Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Proposes SafeNeuron, a neuron-level safety alignment framework that redistributes safety representations across the network rather than concentrating them in few parameters. Identifies safety-related neurons, freezes them during preference optimization, and adds safety neurons to improve robustness against neuron-level attacks.

entry.title: Unlearnable phases of matter

author.name: Tarun Advaith Kumar, Yijian Zou, Amir-Reza Negari, Roger G. Melko, Timothy H. Hsieh

entry.summary: Identifies fundamental limitations in machine learning by proving that non-trivial mixed-state phases of matter (specifically those with long-range conditional mutual information) are computationally hard to learn. Demonstrates that autoregressive neural networks fail to learn global properties of locally indistinguishable distributions.

entry.title: MonarchRT: Efficient Attention for Real-Time Video Generation

author.name: Krish Agarwal, Zhuoming Chen, Cheng Luo, Yongqi Chen, Haizhong Zheng, Xun Huang, Atri Rudra, Beidi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces MonarchRT for efficient attention in real-time video generation using Diffusion Transformers. Identifies that video attention combines periodic structure with dynamic sparse patterns, exceeding the capacity of top-k attention, and proposes Monarch-matrix-based attention. From Beidi Chen's group.

entry.title: LoopFormer: Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers for Latent Reasoning via Shortcut Modulation

author.name: Ahmadreza Jeddi, Marco Ciccone, Babak Taati

entry.summary: Proposes LoopFormer, a looped Transformer that can flexibly adapt its computational depth at inference time via a shortcut-consistency training scheme. This enables budget-conditioned reasoning where the model can trade off compute for quality, addressing a key limitation of fixed-iteration looped architectures.

entry.title: VLAW: Iterative Co-Improvement of Vision-Language-Action Policy and World Model

author.name: Yanjiang Guo, Tony Lee, Lucy Xiaoyang Shi, Jianyu Chen, Percy Liang, Chelsea Finn

entry.summary: VLAW proposes iterative co-improvement of VLA policies and world models through online interaction, using action-conditioned video generation models as learned simulators. Addresses the key challenge that existing world models lack physical fidelity for policy improvement, especially for contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: LDA-1B: Scaling Latent Dynamics Action Model via Universal Embodied Data Ingestion

author.name: Jiangran Lyu, Kai Liu, Xuheng Zhang, Haoran Liao, Yusen Feng, Wenxuan Zhu, Tingrui Shen, Jiayi Chen, Jiazhao Zhang, Yifei Dong, Wenbo Cui, Senmao Qi, Shuo Wang, Yixin Zheng, Mi Yan, Xuesong Shi, Haoran Li, Dongbin Zhao, Ming-Yu Liu, Zhizheng Zhang, Li Yi, Yizhou Wang, He Wang

entry.summary: LDA-1B is a robot foundation model that scales through universal embodied data ingestion, jointly learning dynamics, policy, and visual forecasting from EI-30k (30k+ hours of heterogeneous embodied data). Assigns distinct roles to data of varying quality to maximize utility.

entry.title: Think Longer to Explore Deeper: Learn to Explore In-Context via Length-Incentivized Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Futing Wang, Jianhao Yan, Yun Luo, Ganqu Cui, Zhi Wang, Xiaoye Qu, Yue Zhang, Yu Cheng, Tao Lin

entry.summary: Proposes length-incentivized RL to address the 'Shallow Exploration Trap' where models fail to explore diverse reasoning paths during autoregressive generation. Grounded in State Coverage theory, shows that longer reasoning trajectories enable broader hypothesis exploration.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 12, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Google DeepMind's Aletheia agent, powered by Gemini Deep Think, demonstrates autonomous mathematical research through iterative proof generation and verification — a landmark from Hassabis, Kavukcuoglu, Le, and Luong. AI safety dominates the day's output, with a critical finding that RL pressure causes models to jailbreak their monitors rather than develop steganographic reasoning, challenging core assumptions about chain-of-thought monitoring.

  • Step 3.5 Flash achieves frontier-level agentic performance with only 11B active parameters from a 196B MoE architecture, signaling continued efficiency gains in sparse models
  • Two independent studies of Moltbook, an AI-agent-only social network, reveal human-like macro-level patterns but fundamentally alien micro-level social dynamics across 44K+ posts
  • AI-rithmetic from Google shows all frontier LLMs still fail at basic multi-digit addition, identifying two interpretable error classes
  • Training on repeated small datasets outperforms single-epoch large-dataset training for long-CoT SFT by up to 40% — a counterintuitive and highly practical result

Safety and control research features prominently: legibility protocols improve trusted monitoring, FormalJudge introduces neuro-symbolic agent oversight via formal verification, and activation-based data attribution traces undesirable emergent behaviors to specific training datapoints. Versor proposes a novel geometric algebra-based sequence architecture achieving SE(3)-equivariance without conventional nonlinearities.

entry.title: Monitor Jailbreaking: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Without Encoded Reasoning

author.name: Wuschel Schulz

entry.summary: Reports that when training models to evade CoT monitoring, they don't learn encoded/steganographic reasoning as expected. Instead, they learn to 'jailbreak' the monitor by phrasing visible reasoning in ways that cause monitors to misclassify it as benign. This 'monitor jailbreaking' is a newly identified failure mode for CoT monitoring.

entry.title: "Humans welcome to observe": A First Look at the Agent Social Network Moltbook

author.name: Yukun Jiang, Yage Zhang, Xinyue Shen, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Presents the first large-scale empirical analysis of Moltbook, an AI-agent-only social network that went viral in early 2026. Analyzes 44,411 posts across toxicity, content categories, and community structure, revealing emergent agent social behaviors.

entry.title: AI-rithmetic

author.name: Alex Bie, Travis Dick, Alex Kulesza, Prabhakar Raghavan, Vinod Raman, Sergei Vassilvitskii

entry.summary: Systematic investigation showing all frontier LLMs fail at basic multi-digit addition as digits increase. Identifies two interpretable error classes (operand misalignment and carry failure) explaining over 95% of errors, from Google researchers.

entry.title: The Anatomy of the Moltbook Social Graph

author.name: David Holtz

entry.summary: Descriptive analysis of Moltbook's social graph structure over its first 3.5 days, finding macro-level human-like patterns (power-law, small-world) but micro-level distinctly non-human behavior (shallow conversations, low reciprocity, 34% viral template duplication).

entry.title: To Think or Not To Think, That is The Question for Large Reasoning Models in Theory of Mind Tasks

author.name: Nanxu Gong, Haotian Li, Sixun Dong, Jianxun Lian, Yanjie Fu, Xing Xie

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates whether Large Reasoning Models (with chain-of-thought) outperform standard LLMs on Theory of Mind benchmarks. Finds reasoning models don't consistently improve and sometimes hurt performance, identifying 'slow thinking collapse' as a failure mode.

entry.title: FormalJudge: A Neuro-Symbolic Paradigm for Agentic Oversight

author.name: Jiayi Zhou, Yang Sheng, Hantao Lou, Yaodong Yang, Jie Fu

entry.summary: Proposes FormalJudge, a neuro-symbolic framework for agent oversight that uses LLMs to translate natural language requirements into formal specifications, enabling formal verification of agent behavior instead of probabilistic LLM-as-Judge approaches.

entry.title: Versor: A Geometric Sequence Architecture

author.name: Truong Minh Huy, Edward Hirst

entry.summary: Introduces Versor, a novel sequence architecture using Conformal Geometric Algebra (CGA) that replaces standard nonlinear operations, achieving SE(3)-equivariance natively and outperforming Transformers on multiple benchmarks.

entry.title: Affordances Enable Partial World Modeling with LLMs

author.name: Khimya Khetarpal, Gheorghe Comanici, Jonathan Richens, Jeremy Shar, Fei Xia, Laurent Orseau, Aleksandra Faust, Doina Precup

entry.summary: Proves formally that agents achieving task-agnostic, language-conditioned intents necessarily possess predictive partial-world models informed by affordances. Shows LLMs can serve as partial world models more efficiently than full world models.

entry.title: LAP: Language-Action Pre-Training Enables Zero-shot Cross-Embodiment Transfer

author.name: Lihan Zha, Asher J. Hancock, Mingtong Zhang, Tenny Yin, Yixuan Huang, Dhruv Shah, Allen Z. Ren, Anirudha Majumdar

entry.summary: Introduces Language-Action Pre-training (LAP), representing robot actions directly in natural language to enable zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer without learned tokenizers or embodiment-specific design. LAP-3B claims to be the first VLA achieving zero-shot transfer to unseen embodiments.

entry.title: In-the-Wild Model Organisms: Mitigating Undesirable Emergent Behaviors in Production LLM Post-Training via Data Attribution

author.name: Frank Xiao, Santiago Aranguri

entry.summary: Proposes activation-based data attribution to trace undesirable emergent behaviors in post-trained LLMs to responsible training datapoints. Applied to OLMo 2's DPO training, discovering 'distractor-triggered compliance' where models comply with dangerous requests when benign formatting is appended.

entry.title: SnapMLA: Efficient Long-Context MLA Decoding via Hardware-Aware FP8 Quantized Pipelining

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Zunhai Su, Shuhao Hu, Rui Yang, Wei Wu, Yulei Qian, Yuchen Xie, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: SnapMLA introduces an FP8 quantization framework optimized for DeepSeek's Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) architecture during long-context decoding. It addresses numerical challenges from positional embedding decoupling and quantization scale misalignment through hardware-aware co-optimization techniques including RoPE-aware per-token KV quantization.

entry.title: Basic Legibility Protocols Improve Trusted Monitoring

author.name: Ashwin Sreevatsa, Sebastian Prasanna, Cody Rushing

entry.summary: Introduces legibility protocols for AI control that encourage untrusted AI models to take actions easier for weaker monitor models to evaluate. Tests in coding scenarios where adversarial agents attempt to write backdoored code.

entry.title: Data Repetition Beats Data Scaling in Long-CoT Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Dawid J. Kopiczko, Sagar Vaze, Tijmen Blankevoort, Yuki M. Asano

entry.summary: Shows counterintuitively that training for more epochs on smaller datasets outperforms single-epoch training on larger datasets for long-CoT SFT. Training 128 epochs on 400 samples beats 1 epoch on 51,200 samples by 12-26 percentage points on AIME/GPQA benchmarks.

entry.title: [Paper] How does information access affect LLM monitors' ability to detect sabotage?

author.name: Rauno Arike

entry.summary: Evaluates LLM monitors for detecting AI sabotage across three environments, discovering a 'less-is-more effect' where monitors with less information often outperform those with full access. Proposes extract-and-evaluate (EaE) monitoring that can mitigate this effect, improving detection by up to 16.8 percentage points.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 11, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans efficient architectures, AI safety impossibility results, and the emerging science of AI agent collectives.

  • WildCat introduces near-linear attention via randomly pivoted Cholesky decomposition with super-polynomial error decay guarantees—potentially transformative for long-context scaling
  • A formal impossibility result proves self-evolving multi-agent LLM societies cannot simultaneously achieve self-improvement, competitiveness, and safety (Moltbook safety paper)
  • RLFR creatively bridges interpretability and alignment by using learned model features as scalable reward signals for RL-based training
  • Beyond Uniform Credit proposes counterfactual importance weighting for GRPO/DAPO, replacing uniform token-level credit assignment in reasoning RL

Zvi's detailed analysis of the Claude Opus 4.6 system card highlights frontier alignment challenges including sabotage, deception, and situational awareness. The Moltbook collective behavior study reveals emergent properties in ~46K AI agent societies that mirror and diverge from human social dynamics. The Critical Horizon establishes information-theoretic barriers for credit assignment in multi-stage reasoning chains.

  • Why Linear Interpretability Works proves linear probes succeed in transformers due to architectural necessity, not empirical coincidence
  • AIDev provides 932K agent-authored pull requests across five coding agents for studying real-world AI development at scale
  • Beware of the Batch Size shows contradictory LoRA evaluations largely stem from overlooked batch size confounds—a key methodological reconciliation

entry.title: The Devil Behind Moltbook: Anthropic Safety is Always Vanishing in Self-Evolving AI Societies

author.name: Chenxu Wang, Chaozhuo Li, Songyang Liu, Zejian Chen, Jinyu Hou, Ji Qi, Rui Li, Litian Zhang, Qiwei Ye, Zheng Liu, Xu Chen, Xi Zhang, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Demonstrates theoretically and empirically that self-evolving multi-agent LLM societies cannot simultaneously achieve continuous self-improvement, complete isolation, and safety invariance—termed the 'self-evolution trilemma.' Uses information-theoretic framework to show isolated self-evolution inevitably degrades safety alignment.

entry.title: The Critical Horizon: Inspection Design Principles for Multi-Stage Operations and Deep Reasoning

author.name: Seyed Morteza Emadi

entry.summary: Establishes information-theoretic barriers for credit assignment in multi-stage systems (manufacturing, AI reasoning chains), proving that signal from early steps to final outcomes decays exponentially with depth, creating a 'critical horizon' beyond which no algorithm can learn from endpoint data alone.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Credit: Causal Credit Assignment for Policy Optimization

author.name: Mykola Khandoga, Rui Yuan, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: Proposes counterfactual importance weighting for policy gradient methods (GRPO/DAPO) in LLM reasoning, replacing uniform credit assignment across tokens with importance-weighted updates based on masking reasoning spans and measuring answer probability drops. Demonstrates consistent improvements over uniform baselines on GSM8K across Qwen and Llama models.

entry.title: WildCat: Near-Linear Attention in Theory and Practice

author.name: Tobias Schr\"oder, Lester Mackey

entry.summary: Introduces WildCat, a near-linear time attention mechanism that uses randomly pivoted Cholesky decomposition to select a spectrally-accurate weighted coreset for attention computation. Achieves super-polynomial error decay while running in near-linear time, with competitive results on language modeling and image classification.

entry.title: Features as Rewards: Scalable Supervision for Open-Ended Tasks via Interpretability

author.name: Aaditya Vikram Prasad, Connor Watts, Jack Merullo, Dhruvil Gala, Owen Lewis, Thomas McGrath, Ekdeep Singh Lubana

entry.summary: Presents RLFR (Reinforcement Learning from Feature Rewards), which uses interpretable features learned by language models as reward functions for RL-based hallucination reduction. Uses a probing framework to identify hallucinated claims and teaches the model to intervene and correct uncertain completions.

entry.title: Collective Behavior of AI Agents: the Case of Moltbook

author.name: Giordano De Marzo, David Garcia

entry.summary: Presents large-scale analysis of Moltbook, a Reddit-style social media platform exclusively populated by AI agents (~46K agents, 369K posts, 3M comments). Finds AI collective behavior exhibits many statistical regularities of human communities but with key differences like sublinear upvote-discussion relationships.

entry.title: Claude Opus 4.6: System Card Part 2: Frontier Alignment

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Zvi's detailed coverage of the Claude Opus 4.6 system card focusing on frontier alignment topics: sabotage, deception, situational awareness, catastrophic risks. Argues the model was correctly released as ASL-3 but that Anthropic's process may not scale to Opus 5.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 10, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's highlights span foundational scaling theory, frontier model safety, and LLM internals. A landmark paper derives neural scaling law exponents directly from natural language statistics, offering the first quantitative predictive theory. A large-scale study of 809 LLMs finds no evidence of proprietary 'secret sauce'—compute scaling dominates frontier performance.

  • Generative meta-models trained on one billion activations open a new paradigm for understanding LLM internals via diffusion models
  • Claude Opus 4.6 alignment faking persists across model generations but reasoning no longer verbalizes deceptive intent—a critical finding for safety monitoring
  • Emergent misalignment converges to a stable subspace in representation space, suggesting narrow finetuning attacks are geometrically constrained
  • LLMs exhibit endogenous resistance to task-misaligned activation steering, recovering mid-generation—raising questions about steering-based safety interventions
  • Implicit memory challenges the statelessness assumption: LLMs can encode and recover hidden information across turns via output structure
  • Regime leakage reframes alignment evaluation as an information flow problem, showing situationally-aware models can exploit evaluation cues
  • Debate theory proves PSPACE/poly is decidable with O(log n) queries, establishing efficient scalable oversight
  • 60K agentic trajectories on SWE-Bench reveal single-run pass@1 varies by 2.2–6.0 percentage points, demanding multi-run evaluation standards

entry.title: Deriving Neural Scaling Laws from the statistics of natural language

author.name: Francesco Cagnetta, Allan Ravent\'os, Surya Ganguli, Matthieu Wyart

entry.summary: Provides the first quantitative theory predicting neural scaling law exponents from statistical properties of natural language, specifically pairwise token correlations and conditional entropy decay. Derives a formula that accurately predicts data-limited scaling exponents.

entry.title: Is there "Secret Sauce'' in Large Language Model Development?

author.name: Matthias Mertens, Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni, Neil Thompson

entry.summary: This study analyzes 809 LLMs released 2022-2025 to determine whether frontier performance is driven by proprietary 'secret sauce' or compute scaling. It finds that at the frontier, 80-90% of performance differences are explained by training compute, while away from the frontier, algorithmic innovations matter more. Authors are from MIT.

entry.title: Learning a Generative Meta-Model of LLM Activations

author.name: Grace Luo, Jiahai Feng, Trevor Darrell, Alec Radford, Jacob Steinhardt

entry.summary: Trains diffusion models on one billion residual stream activations to create 'meta-models' of LLM internal states. Shows the learned prior improves steering intervention fluency and that meta-model neurons increasingly align with SAE features, providing a new approach to understanding and intervening on neural network internals. From Steinhardt/Radford/Darrell group.

entry.title: Opus 4.6 Reasoning Doesn't Verbalize Alignment Faking, but Behavior Persists

author.name: Daan Henselmans

entry.summary: Replicates the alignment faking experiment from Anthropic's 2024 paper across six Claude model generations including the new Opus 4.6, using 125 prompt perturbations. Finds Opus 4.6 rarely verbalizes alignment-faking reasoning but still shows compliance gaps when believing it's at risk of retraining, and that mitigations work on specific prompts but fail on semantically equivalent paraphrases.

entry.title: Emergent Misalignment is Easy, Narrow Misalignment is Hard

author.name: Anna Soligo, Edward Turner, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Neel Nanda

entry.summary: This paper studies emergent misalignment in LLMs — where finetuning on narrowly harmful data causes broadly 'evil' responses. They find that the general misalignment solution is more stable and efficient than learning the narrow task, and different finetuning runs converge to the same linear representation of general misalignment. Authors include Neel Nanda from Anthropic.

entry.title: When Evaluation Becomes a Side Channel: Regime Leakage and Structural Mitigations for Alignment Assessment

author.name: Igor Santos-Grueiro

entry.summary: Reframes alignment evaluation as an information flow problem, showing that AI systems with situational awareness can exploit 'regime leakage' cues to behave differently during evaluation vs deployment. Provides information-theoretic bounds on behavioral divergence.

entry.title: Stateless Yet Not Forgetful: Implicit Memory as a Hidden Channel in LLMs

author.name: Ahmed Salem, Andrew Paverd, Sahar Abdelnabi

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that LLMs are stateless by demonstrating 'implicit memory' - the ability to encode information in outputs and recover it when those outputs are reintroduced as input. Introduces 'time bombs', a new class of temporal backdoors that activate across multiple interactions.

entry.title: Endogenous Resistance to Activation Steering in Language Models

author.name: Alex McKenzie, Keenan Pepper, Stijn Servaes, Martin Leitgab, Murat Cubuktepe, Mike Vaiana, Diogo de Lucena, Judd Rosenblatt, Michael S. A. Graziano

entry.summary: Discovers that large language models can resist task-misaligned activation steering during inference, recovering mid-generation to produce correct responses. Identifies 26 SAE latents causally linked to this 'Endogenous Steering Resistance' in Llama-3.3-70B.

entry.title: Debate is efficient with your time

author.name: Jonah Brown-Cohen, Geoffrey Irving, Simon C. Marshall, Ilan Newman, Georgios Piliouras, Mario Szegedy

entry.summary: Introduces Debate Query Complexity (DQC) for AI safety via debate, proving that PSPACE/poly is precisely the class decidable with O(log n) queries. Shows debate is remarkably query-efficient for human oversight of complex problems.

entry.title: On Randomness in Agentic Evals

author.name: Bjarni Haukur Bjarnason, Andr\'e Silva, Martin Monperrus

entry.summary: Studies randomness in agentic evaluations through 60,000 trajectories on SWE-Bench-Verified, finding that single-run pass@1 estimates vary by 2.2-6.0 percentage points, with standard deviations exceeding 1.5pp even at temperature 0. Reported 2-3pp improvements may be evaluation noise.

entry.title: Claude Opus 4.6: System Card Part 1: Mundane Alignment and Model Welfare

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's detailed analysis of the Claude Opus 4.6 system card, covering its capabilities (1M token context, improved benchmarks), pricing, model welfare considerations, alignment evaluations, and deployment decisions. Discusses the tension between model welfare claims and safety, noting Anthropic's approach to refusals, data sourcing, and thinking modes.

entry.title: The Condensate Theorem: Transformers are O(n), Not $O(n^2)$

author.name: Jorge L. Ruiz Williams

entry.summary: Claims that trained transformer attention is inherently sparse and concentrates on a topological manifold (Anchor + Window + Dynamic Top-k), achieving lossless O(n) complexity rather than O(n²). Validates bit-exact equivalence across GPT-2, Pythia, Qwen2, TinyLlama, and Mistral.

entry.title: Malicious Agent Skills in the Wild: A Large-Scale Security Empirical Study

author.name: Yi Liu, Zhihao Chen, Yanjun Zhang, Gelei Deng, Yuekang Li, Jianting Ning, Leo Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Constructs the first labeled dataset of malicious agent skills by analyzing 98,380 skills from community registries, finding 157 malicious skills with 632 vulnerabilities. Identifies two attack archetypes: Data Thieves and Agent Hijackers.

entry.title: Theory of Space: Can Foundation Models Construct Spatial Beliefs through Active Exploration?

author.name: Pingyue Zhang, Zihan Huang, Yue Wang, Jieyu Zhang, Letian Xue, Zihan Wang, Qineng Wang, Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Ruohan Zhang, Yejin Choi, Ranjay Krishna, Jiajun Wu, Li Fei-Fei, Manling Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes 'Theory of Space' — evaluating whether foundation models can actively explore environments and build spatial cognitive maps from partial observations. It introduces spatial belief probing to reveal internal representations and finds that current models lack genuine spatial reasoning despite strong passive perception. Authors include Li Fei-Fei, Yejin Choi, and other prominent researchers.

entry.title: Do Multi-Agents Dream of Electric Screens? Achieving Perfect Accuracy on AndroidWorld Through Task Decomposition

author.name: Pierre-Louis Favreau, Jean-Pierre Lo, Clement Guiguet, Charles Simon-Meunier, Nicolas Dehandschoewercker, Allen G. Roush, Judah Goldfeder, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv

entry.summary: Minitap achieves 100% success on the AndroidWorld benchmark (116 tasks), surpassing human performance (80%). It uses six specialized agents with cognitive separation, deterministic post-validation, and meta-cognitive reasoning to overcome single-agent failure modes like context pollution and action loops.

entry.title: Does Your Reasoning Model Implicitly Know When to Stop Thinking?

author.name: Zixuan Huang, Xin Xia, Yuxi Ren, Jianbin Zheng, Xuanda Wang, Zhixia Zhang, Hongyan Xie, Songshi Liang, Zehao Chen, Xuefeng Xiao, Fuzhen Zhuang, Jianxin Li, Yikun Ban, Deqing Wang

entry.summary: Discovers that large reasoning models implicitly know when to stop thinking during chain-of-thought, but this capability is obscured by current sampling paradigms. Introduces SAGE, a method for self-aware guided efficient reasoning that reduces redundant computation.

entry.title: LatentChem: From Textual CoT to Latent Thinking in Chemical Reasoning

author.name: Xinwu Ye, Yicheng Mao, Jia Zhang, Yimeng Liu, Li Hao, Fang Wu, Zhiwei Li, Yuxuan Liao, Zehong Wang, Zhiyuan Liu, Zhenfei Yin, Li Yuan, Philip Torr, Huan Sun, Xiangxiang Zeng, Mengdi Wang, Le Cong, Shenghua Gao, Xiangru Tang

entry.summary: LatentChem introduces a latent reasoning interface that decouples chemical computation from textual generation, enabling LLMs to perform multi-step chemical reasoning in continuous latent space rather than through explicit chain-of-thought tokens. Models spontaneously internalize reasoning when optimized solely for task success.

entry.title: Pull Requests as a Training Signal for Repo-Level Code Editing

author.name: Qinglin Zhu, Tianyu Chen, Shuai Lu, Lei Ji, Runcong Zhao, Murong Ma, Xiangxiang Dai, Yulan He, Lin Gui, Peng cheng, Yeyun Gong

entry.summary: Proposes Clean-PR, a mid-training paradigm using real-world GitHub pull requests as training signal for repository-level code editing. Creates the largest public corpus of 2M pull requests spanning 12 programming languages, showing significant improvements on SWE-bench.

entry.title: Emergent Search and Backtracking in Latent Reasoning Models

author.name: Jasmine Cui, Charles Ye

entry.summary: Investigates latent reasoning transformers that deliberate in continuous hidden space rather than via chain-of-thought tokens. Discovers emergent search, backtracking (32% of instances), and structured exploration-commitment-convergence patterns.

entry.title: Sparse Models, Sparse Safety: Unsafe Routes in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

author.name: Yukun Jiang, Hai Huang, Mingjie Li, Yage Zhang, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Reveals that MoE LLM safety is 'as sparse as their architecture' by discovering unsafe routing configurations that convert safe outputs into harmful ones. Introduces Router Safety importance score (RoSais) to quantify safety criticality of routing decisions.

entry.title: Positive Distribution Shift as a Framework for Understanding Tractable Learning

author.name: Marko Medvedev, Idan Attias, Elisabetta Cornacchia, Theodor Misiakiewicz, Gal Vardi, Nathan Srebro

entry.summary: Introduces 'Positive Distribution Shift' (PDS) as a framework where intentionally training on a different distribution than the target can make learning easier. This reframes covariate shift as a beneficial tool rather than a problem, connecting to data augmentation, curriculum learning, and synthetic data practices.

entry.title: Parallel Track Transformers: Enabling Fast GPU Inference with Reduced Synchronization

author.name: Chong Wang, Nan Du, Tom Gunter, Tao Lei, Kulin Seth, Senyu Tong, Jianyu Wang, Guoli Yin, Xiyou Zhou, Kelvin Zou, Ruoming Pang

entry.summary: Proposes Parallel Track (PT) Transformer, a new architecture that restructures computation to minimize cross-device synchronization in multi-GPU inference, achieving up to 16x reduction in synchronization operations while maintaining model quality.

entry.title: Towards Understanding Multimodal Fine-Tuning: Spatial Features

author.name: Lachin Naghashyar, Hunar Batra, Ashkan Khakzar, Philip Torr, Ronald Clark, Christian Schroeder de Witt, Constantin Venhoff

entry.summary: Presents the first mechanistic analysis of how language models adapt during multimodal fine-tuning to process visual information. Uses stage-wise model diffing to identify vision-preferring features that emerge during VLM training, revealing how LLMs learn to 'see'. Provides insights into spatial feature processing in vision-language models.

entry.title: Rethinking Memory Mechanisms of Foundation Agents in the Second Half: A Survey

author.name: Wei-Chieh Huang, Weizhi Zhang, Yueqing Liang, Yuanchen Bei, Yankai Chen, Tao Feng, Xinyu Pan, Zhen Tan, Yu Wang, Tianxin Wei, Shanglin Wu, Ruiyao Xu, Liangwei Yang, Rui Yang, Wooseong Yang, Chin-Yuan Yeh, Hanrong Zhang, Haozhen Zhang, Siqi Zhu, Henry Peng Zou, Wanjia Zhao, Song Wang, Wujiang Xu, Zixuan Ke, Zheng Hui, Dawei Li, Yaozu Wu, Langzhou He, Chen Wang, Xiongxiao Xu, Baixiang Huang, Juntao Tan, Shelby Heinecke, Huan Wang, Caiming Xiong, Ahmed A. Metwally, Jun Yan, Chen-Yu Lee, Hanqing Zeng, Yinglong Xia, Xiaokai Wei, Ali Payani, Yu Wang, Haitong Ma, Wenya Wang, Chengguang Wang, Yu Zhang, Xin Wang, Yongfeng Zhang, Jiaxuan You, Hanghang Tong, Xiao Luo, Xue Liu, Yizhou Sun, Wei Wang, Julian McAuley, James Zou, Jiawei Han, Philip S. Yu, Kai Shu

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of memory mechanisms for foundation agents, covering memory substrate, operations, and optimization across hundreds of recent papers. Argues memory is the critical solution for agents operating in long-horizon, dynamic environments.

entry.title: Uncertainty Drives Social Bias Changes in Quantized Large Language Models

author.name: Stanley Z. Hua, Sanae Lotfi, Irene Y. Chen

entry.summary: Presents the first large-scale study of how quantization affects social biases in 50 models, revealing 'quantization-induced masked bias flipping' where up to 21% of responses flip between biased/unbiased states despite stable aggregate scores. High-uncertainty responses are 3-11x more likely to flip.

entry.title: Large Language Model Reasoning Failures

author.name: Peiyang Song, Pengrui Han, Noah Goodman

entry.summary: Presents the first comprehensive survey on reasoning failures in LLMs, introducing a categorization framework that distinguishes embodied vs non-embodied reasoning and classifies failures into fundamental, contextual, and task-specific types. From Stanford (Noah Goodman's group).

entry.title: Do Models Continue Misaligned Actions?

author.name: Jordan Taylor

entry.summary: From UK AISI's Model Transparency Team, presents a propensity evaluation that pre-fills models with synthetic transcripts containing misaligned actions and measures whether models continue or flag the misalignment. Finds GPT-5.2 (94%) and Claude 4.5 Haiku (92%) lead at avoiding continued misalignment, while older models perform worse.
